## Summary
Define the core persisted models in `BlauPersistence` as `SchemaV1: VersionedSchema`, following the CloudKit constraints.

## Implementation notes
- `Conversation` (id: UUID = .init(), startedAt, endedAt?, title?, topics: [Topic]? (cascade), utterances: [Utterance]? (cascade)).
- `Topic` (id, conversation?, startedAt, endedAt?, title (default "New topic"), titleIsProvisional (Bool), summary?, ordinal, utterances: [Utterance]? (nullify), colorSeed).
- `Utterance` (id, conversation?, topic?, roleRaw ("user" / "agent" / "system"), text, startedAt, endedAt?, asrConfidence?, voiceScore?, isFinal, sourceRaw ("parakeet" / "speechanalyzer" / "grok")).
- `VoiceProfile` (id, name, embeddingModelVersion, centroid (`Data`), createdAt, updatedAt, enrollmentSets: [VoiceEnrollmentSet]? (cascade)) and `VoiceEnrollmentSet` (profile?, deviceModel, embeddings (`Data`, packed Float32 × 256), clipCount, createdAt). **Synced via CloudKit** (product decision: the voiceprint syncs).
- CloudKit rules: every attribute optional or defaulted, **no `@Attribute(.unique)`**, all relationships optional with explicit inverses, no `.deny`. Enums are stored as raw strings.
- Flat models, no `@Model` inheritance (CloudKit cast crashes reported on iOS 26.x).
- `BlauMigrationPlan: SchemaMigrationPlan` with `[SchemaV1]` from day one.

### Still needs physical-device or manual verification

- Results table for ≥2 devices committed: no physical iPhone here. The table in docs/benchmarks.md is committed with every iPhone cell marked pending; `make bench DEVICE=<udid>` fills it.
- Clear go/no-go on EOU-320 as the default: the rule is in code, but the verdict is pending until two iPhones report. EOU-320 stays the provisional default.
- Background-ANE behaviour documented with a mitigation decision: the SDK findings and the mitigation table are committed, but the probe has not been run on a locked iOS 27 iPhone, so it is not yet known whether Core ML errors, falls back to the CPU, or keeps working.
- EmbeddingGemma latency: no Core ML conversion of the model exists in the repo or any package, so that case skips until one is supplied (#59).
- The benchmark screen has only been checked on a simulator by screenshot; running models through it on a phone has not been tried.

### Unresolved reviewer concerns

- After the rebase onto #99, the debug benchmark screen and the background probe can't download their models. The app calls SpeechModels.makeManager() (Blau/SpeechModels/SpeechModels.swift:43) on every live launch, and that sets ModelHub.offlineMode = true through FluidAudioModels.disableImplicitDownloads(). From then on, ParakeetEouChunkProcessor.prepare (Packages/BlauKit/Sources/BlauTranscription/Benchmarks/ParakeetEouChunkProcessor.swift:83, ModelHub.download) throws networkDisabled. AsrModels.download (ParakeetTdtEngine.swift:29) and DiarizerModels/CampPlusModels.download (FluidAudioSpeakerExtractors.swift:31,71) throw modelMissing. I confirmed this with a throwaway test: after disableImplicitDownloads(), prepare threw networkDisabled(operation: "download(parakeet-eou-streaming/320ms)"). Because of this, the in-app background ANE probe fails at its CPU-baseline step (BackgroundInferenceProbe.swift:103), and that probe is the only tool for the background-ANE acceptance criterion. Every EOU, TDT and speaker case on the screen fails too. Fix, either: (a) load from ModelManager.directory(for:) by adding a modelDirectory init to ParakeetEouChunkProcessor; or (b) add a scoped FluidAudioModels.withImplicitDownloads helper that turns offline mode off for the debug screen's runs and restores it in the tasks' defer blocks. Add a hermetic test.
- The background probe catches up after a freeze, so a suspension the app resumes from while still off screen is cancelled out and can read as .works (BackgroundInferenceProbe.swift:174-177). After a G-second freeze, the loop runs every missed step back to back. Each of those burst samples counts as a full expectedInterval in coverage, so coverage comes out at about T/(T+G), which is always above 0.5. Those catch-up windows are also timed in burst rather than paced. Reproduced with VirtualClock and FakeStreamingProcessor: lock at 15 s, freeze for 400 s at 30 s, stay locked, 600 s run. The probe reported coverage 0.58, .works(slowdown: 1.0) and keepNeuralEngine, and 1,382 of the 1,772 locked samples were catch-up bursts. Fix: at the top of the loop, `let due = Int((context.clock.uptime - start) / hop); if due > step { step = due }`. With that change the same scenario gives .suspended(0.31), and all 11 existing probe and analysis tests still pass. Add this scenario as a regression test.

## Summary
Play Grok's streamed audio deltas smoothly and stop instantly on barge-in.

## Implementation notes
- `AVAudioPlayerNode` on the same engine as capture (so echo cancellation sees the reference signal). Decode base64 PCM16 (or binary frames) into `AVAudioPCMBuffer` at 24 kHz and convert to the output format.

- Track **played milliseconds per response item** (needed for `conversation.item.truncate`).
- `flush()` stops the node and drops queued buffers within one IO cycle.
- Output level stream (agent speaking indicator). Signpost `playback.firstBuffer`.

- [ ] Gapless playback of a recorded 2-minute delta stream
- [ ] flush() → silence < 50 ms
- [ ] Played-ms accurate to ±20 ms against the test fixture

## Summary
Real-time transcription of the user's speech with low-latency partials and end-of-utterance events.

## Implementation notes
- Define `protocol Transcriber { func start() async throws; var events: AsyncStream<TranscriptEvent> }` with events `.partial(text, range)`, `.final(Utterance)`.
- `ParakeetStreamingTranscriber` wraps `StreamingEouAsrManager(chunkSize: .ms320, eouDebounceMs: ~800)`: `setPartialCallback`, `setEouCallback`, token timestamps.
- **Call `finish()` / `reset()` after every EOU.** Otherwise the accumulated tokens grow and every partial re-decodes the whole history.
- VAD speechEnd acts as a fallback commit when no EOU arrives. Max utterance length guard.
- Wrap per-chunk work in `autoreleasepool`. Signposts `asr.chunk`, `asr.eou`.
- Adaptive chunk size (320 → 1280 ms) via the thermal policy hook.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Partial text visible < 400 ms after speech on A17+
- [ ] EOU → final utterance < 1.2 s after the user stops
- [ ] 1-hour fixture replay: flat memory, no growth in per-chunk latency

## Summary
Connect to xAI straight from the phone, with no backend. The user's API key lives in the Keychain and the app mints short-lived realtime tokens itself.

## Implementation notes
- `APIKeyStore`: keeps the xAI API key in the Keychain with `kSecAttrSynchronizable = true` (syncs to the user's other devices through iCloud Keychain) and `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock` (readable during locked-screen background sessions). Never stored in UserDefaults or SwiftData, and never logged.
- Entry points: Settings → xAI account and onboarding. Validate with a cheap authenticated call (such as `GET https://api.x.ai/v1/models`). Show clear errors for invalid or unfunded keys.
- `TokenProvider` actor: `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/realtime/client_secrets` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `{"expires_after":{"seconds":600},"session":{"model":"grok-voice-think-fast-2.0"}}`. Caches `{value, expires_at}`, refreshes ~60 s before expiry, retries with backoff.
- The WebSocket authenticates with the subprotocol `xai-client-secret.<token>`, because `URLSessionWebSocketTask` strips the `Authorization` header on the upgrade.
- `XAIHTTPClient` for REST calls (topic-label fallback, fact extraction) uses the Keychain key directly.
- DEBUG: `XAI_DEV_API_KEY` from `Secrets.xcconfig` pre-fills the Keychain on first launch.
- Out of scope: if Blau ever ships publicly on a shared xAI account, a minting proxy can sit behind `TokenProvider` without changing callers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No API key in the app binary or the repo
- [ ] A key entered on one device is available on the user's other devices
- [ ] Token refresh covered by unit tests with a fake clock
- [ ] An invalid key shows a recoverable error in Settings and onboarding

## Summary
A pure-Swift, deterministic, unit-tested engine that decides when the conversation moved to a new topic.

## Implementation notes
- Unit = one finalized exchange (user utterance + agent reply). Embedding via `TextEmbedder` protocol: start with `NLContextualEmbedding` (mean-pooled), swap to the shared EmbeddingGemma service in M3.
- At each gap: `sim = cos(mean(prev 3 units), mean(next 2 units))`. Keep a running μ/σ. TextTiling depth = (leftPeak − sim) + (rightPeak − sim).
- Candidate when depth > μ + kσ (k≈1.0) **and** sustained for 2 more units **and** the current topic is ≥ 4 units / 60 s **and** ≥ 30 s since the last boundary. Exit hysteresis on recovery above a higher threshold.
- The boundary is placed retroactively at the deepest dip. Explicit cues ("let's switch gears", "new topic") boost the score.
- All parameters live in `TopicConfig`. Output events: `.candidate(at:)`, `.confirmed(boundary)`, `.rejected`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests on scripted transcripts with labelled boundaries (Pk / WindowDiff metrics)
- [ ] No flapping on a fixture with a brief digression

## Summary
The signature UI. Each topic is a bullet on a vertical timeline, and every topic label auto-updates.

## Implementation notes
**Interaction (confirmed by the product owner):**
1. On open, the screen is anchored to the **current topic**. The timeline of topic bullets (dot + auto-label + time) starts **above the fold**. Only the current topic is expanded, with its live transcript below its bullet.
2. **Older topics are compressed:** one row each (dot + auto-label + time + duration), no transcript, until the user taps them.
3. **Swipe down** (pull content down) reveals the history: compressed bullets on a continuous vertical rail, newest at the bottom, grouped by day / conversation.
4. **Tap a compressed bullet** to expand it inline (see #58). Tap again to compress it.
5. Swiping back (or tapping the current bullet / a "Now" pill) returns to the current topic with a spring animation.

**Implementation:**
- `ScrollView { LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]) { ForEach(topics) { Section(header: TopicBullet) { … } } }.scrollTargetLayout() }` with `.defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom)` and `.defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom, for: .sizeChanges)`, `.scrollPosition($position)`.
- **No inverted ScrollView** (it breaks VoiceOver and context menus).
- Rail + dots drawn with an `.overlay(alignment: .leading)` / `Canvas`. The current topic's dot pulses while recording. Provisional titles are in italics and cross-fade when refined.
- Compressed rows have a fixed height (cheap layout, stable scroll offsets). Expansion state is view state (`Set<Topic.ID>`), not persisted; everything except the current topic is compressed on launch.
- A label change animates in place (`contentTransition(.numericText())`-style text transition).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Opens on the current topic with bullets visible above the fold
- [ ] Older topics render as compressed single-row bullets until tapped; only the current topic is expanded by default
- [ ] Swipe down reveals older topics; swipe back / tap Now returns
- [ ] Auto-label updates animate without scroll jumps
- [ ] VoiceOver reads the timeline as a list of topics with times

- [ ] #54 Manage the topic lifecycle: open, provisional title, refine on close, manual edits
- [ ] #42 Build the chat transcript view: user text right-aligned, agent text left-aligned, no bubbles

## Summary
Barge-in (#37) asks to "mark the agent utterance as interrupted in the UI and storage". The UI part is done: `TurnSnapshot.interruptedAgentUtterances` feeds the chat transcript (#42). The storage part isn't. The mark lives only in memory and is cleared on every `TurnOrchestrator.start()`, so after a relaunch, in history, in exports and on other devices, a cut-short reply looks like a complete one. The stored row is cut to what was heard (its text and `endedAt`), but nothing records that it was cut.

This came up in the PR #123 review (round 1, item 4; round 2, item 3) and again in the post-merge audit of #37.

- Add an additive, optional field to the stored `Utterance`, for example `isInterrupted: Bool?` or a raw `endReasonRaw: String?` (completed / interrupted / bargedIn), in a new `SchemaV3` that copies v2 unchanged. Add a lightweight `migrateV2toV3` stage to `BlauMigrationPlan` and extend `CloudKitCompatibility` (docs/data-model.md).
- Write it from `TurnOrchestrator.abandon` for the items it adds to `interruptedAgentUtterances` (through `TurnTranscriptRecording`), and read it in the transcript, timeline history and Markdown export.
- Deploy the schema to the CloudKit production environment before shipping a build that writes it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A reply cut off by barge-in or by a new utterance is still shown as interrupted after a relaunch and on a second device

## Summary
Two concerns from the #62 review are valid but were deferred from #164. Both change the memory-eval key texts, so `MemoryEvalRetrievalTests` fails until the eval vectors are recorded again, and recording needs the Python embedding environment and a model download. Neither fits a hermetic PR. Fix both in one PR so the vectors and the baseline are recorded once.

### N3: invalidated facts are folded into the exchange `facts:` prefix
An exchange's key text is `[date] [topic] facts: a; b`. Both chunking paths add **every** fact whose `sourceUtteranceID` is in the exchange, including facts with `invalidatedAt` set:
- `MemoryIndexRebuilder.rebuild` (`factsByUtterance`, `Packages/BlauKit/Sources/BlauMemory/Index/MemoryIndexRebuilder.swift`)
- `MemoryIndexer.conversationSources` (`statements`, `Packages/BlauKit/Sources/BlauMemory/Indexing/MemoryIndexer.swift`)

A superseded statement ("User lives in Berlin") then keeps boosting the exchange for queries about the old value, and it fills one of the `maximumFactsPerExchange` slots.

**Code change.** In both paths, skip a fact's *statement* when `invalidatedAt != nil`, but keep its id in `factIDsByUtterance` / `factIDs` (`linkedFactIDs`, table `fact_link`). That way an un-invalidated or edited fact still re-chunks its exchange. Variant to decide on: keep it as `<statement> (until <date>)` instead of dropping it. That changes the same keys. Bump the indexer's chunking fingerprint (`"v1 …"` → `"v2 …"` in `MemoryIndexer.chunkingFingerprint`) so existing indexes get one full pass. Test: an exchange with one valid and one invalidated fact has only the valid statement in its key, in both the rebuilder and the indexer, and the indexer still matches a from-scratch rebuild.

### N6: `ApproximateTokenCounter` undercounts digit-heavy and non-Latin text
`ApproximateTokenCounter.tokenCount` (`Packages/BlauKit/Sources/BlauMemory/Index/ChunkingPolicy.swift`) is `(utf8.count + 3) / 4 + overhead`. For text full of numbers, or for CJK and other text that takes 3 or more bytes per scalar, this can be lower than the model's real count. A chunk that fits the estimate can then go past the model's sequence length and be truncated when it is embedded. `ChunkingPolicy.forSequenceLength` leaves only 1/8 for the error.

**Code change.** A more conservative estimate was tried in #164 (then reverted): one token per ASCII digit and one per Unicode scalar of 3 or more bytes, plus bytes / 4 for the rest. Changing the counter changes chunk boundaries, so bump the chunking fingerprint as for N3. `ProfileBlock.approximateTokenCount` uses the same bytes / 4 rule. Decide whether it should change too.

**Not verified:** the claim that EmbeddingGemma's tokenizer splits digits into one token each comes from Gemma's published tokenizer description. It has **not** been checked against the model's `tokenizer.json`. The `Fixtures/Tokenizers/gemma-like` fixture is synthetic and can't settle it. Before choosing the rule, compare the estimate with `TextEmbeddingModel.tokenCount(of:as:)` on the real tokenizer for digit-heavy, CJK and emoji samples. That needs the gated model files, so do it off CI. Then add a hermetic test that the estimate is at least the measured count for those samples, with the measured counts written into the test.

## Re-record and update the baseline
Follow [docs/memory-eval.md](../blob/main/docs/memory-eval.md) ("Recording vectors" and "Updating the baseline"):
1. Export the new key texts: `cd Packages/BlauKit && BLAU_MEMORY_EVAL_EXPORT=/tmp/memory-eval-texts.json swift test --filter MemoryEvalExportTests`
2. Re-record **`Packages/BlauKit/Tests/BlauMemoryTests/Fixtures/MemoryEvalVectors/qwen3-embedding-0.6b-256d-int8.json`** with `scripts/embeddings/record_memory_eval_vectors.py` (the Python environment is in `docs/benchmarks.md`).
3. Update the baseline: `make eval-memory MEMORY_EVAL_GATE=0`, then copy the report to **`docs/memory-eval/baseline.json`** and `docs/memory-eval/report.md`. Update **`docs/memory-eval/thresholds.json`** if the numbers move, and add a row to History in `docs/memory-eval.md`. N6 can change the chunk count (`dataset.chunks`, 259 today), which `theBaselineMatchesTheDataset` checks.
4. Remove the known-issue test `MemoryIndexRebuilderTests.anInvalidatedFactIsLeftOutOfItsExchangeKey` (added in #164). Once N3 is fixed, its `withKnownIssue` block fails because the issue no longer occurs, so it has to be replaced by a real test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Invalidated statements are not in exchange keys, in both the rebuilder and the indexer. Fact links are kept.
- [ ] The token estimate is checked against the real EmbeddingGemma tokenizer on digit-heavy and non-Latin text, and it is not lower than the real count on those samples.
- [ ] The chunking fingerprint is bumped.
- [ ] The memory-eval vectors, baseline and thresholds are re-recorded. `MemoryEvalRetrievalTests` passes.
